_readme: MONEY-1359 — Largest Contentful Paint, p75, against Google's 2.5s 'good'
boundary. The regression alarm the performance week reads its baseline from.
p75 and not p95, because that is the percentile Core Web Vitals is DEFINED
on: it is what Search reports and what the 2.5s number means. Alerting on a
p95 against a p75 threshold would fire on a page that Google calls good.
_units_rationale: THE THRESHOLD IS IN NANOSECONDS, and this is the single most likely thing in
this directory to be wrong by a factor of a million.
in NANOSECONDS. 2.5s is therefore 2_500_000_000. Written as a plain integer
because Datadog rejects an expression here.
Get it wrong low and the monitor fires on every page forever; wrong high and
it never fires and nobody notices, because a silent monitor and a healthy one
look identical. That is the MONEY-1238 shape, and unlike the metric-name
version of it there is no series to check the name of — the query is valid
So apply-service-monitors.sh does not merely preflight that VIEWS EXIST: it
prints the observed p75 next to the threshold when it applies this row. An
can see the magnitude is right; `observed p75 = 1840` against the same
threshold says the unit assumption is wrong, in one line, at apply time
rather than after a month of silence.
name: [{{env}}] stockbook-web — LCP p75 over 2.5s for 30 minutes
message:
stockbook-web's LCP p75 stayed above 2.5s for 30 minutes — the boundary Core Web Vitals calls 'good'.

Threshold is in NANOSECONDS (2_500_000_000). RUM view timings are stored in ns; a threshold written in ms would be a million times too small and this monitor would never stop firing.

RUM Explorer: `@type:view service:stockbook-web env:{{env}}`, pc75 of `@view.largest_contentful_paint`, grouped by `@view.url_path` — a site-wide rise is usually the shell or a font; one route is that route's data fetch.

30 minutes, not 15: LCP is noisy per-session and a shorter window fires on a handful of slow connections.

@{{notify}}
_notify_no_data_rationale: FALSE, same as the RUM error row: no sessions is a normal overnight state,
